chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Matt al-Jawhari narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from 'Ali ibn al-NuAli ibn al-Nu'man, from 'Abdillah ibn Muskān, who said:

Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Allāh, the Blessed and the Exalted, manifests (His Mercy) to the Zuwwār of the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him) before the people of 'Arafāt. He fulfils their needs, forgives their sins, and accepts their intercession for their requests. Thereafter, He attends to the people of 'Arafāt and honours them in the same way.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of visitors to the grave of Imam al-Husain on the Day of 'Arafah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the unique spiritual status of the Ziyarah of Imam al-Husain (a.s.) by positioning it as a precursor to the supreme act of worship at 'Arafah, where divine manifestation (Tajalli) occurs earlier for the visitors. It underscores the concept of 'Shafa'ah' (intercession) and the fulfillment of needs, reflecting the Shia belief in the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt as mediators of divine mercy. The comparison with 'Ahl al-'Arafah' elevates the grave visitation to a level of near-equality with the Hajj pilgrimage in terms of spiritual reward and divine attention.
